To determine which technique is commonly used to study reactions occurring on timescales of milliseconds to seconds, let's consider each option:

A. Flash photolysis - This technique is typically used for very fast reactions, often in the microsecond range, so it might not be the best fit for millisecond to second timescales.

B. NMR spectroscopy - While NMR can be used to study reactions, it is not specifically known for studying reactions on millisecond to second timescales.

C. Shock tubes - These are used to study very fast processes and are not typically associated with millisecond to second timescales.

D. Stopped-flow method - This technique is specifically designed to monitor the progress of reactions on a millisecond to second timescale.
